A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of optimal and greedy decision trees. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from v1's main text into v2's appendices.

before.justification: Sections 3–5 report original objective-function, tuning, accuracy, interpretability, and runtime experiments using an OpenML benchmark and generated synthetic data.

after.justification: Sections 3–5 retain original empirical comparisons and add experiments. Appendices B and D also report tuning-budget, training-accuracy, and binarization analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed methodological set is substantially narrowed. Error Gini and Error entropy, introduced in v1 Section 3.3, are removed, leaving M-loss and L-loss. G-Test threshold tuning is also removed, reducing the new tuning approaches from three to two. The retained losses, question-length tuning, smoothing, and STreeD framework remain.

E1.justification: The OpenML benchmark changes from 165 to 180 datasets through substantial membership changes, including additions such as compas-two-years, mushroom, and PhishingWebsites. V2 also introduces synthetic classification with linear ground-truth separators, extending coverage beyond tree-generated ground truths. Electricity, Covertype, and Higgs were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Error Gini and Error entropy disappear from the ODT and greedy objective comparisons, and G-Test threshold tuning disappears from the tuning comparison. Conversely, the SWA comparison expands from Accuracy, Binom., and CART in v1 Table 3 to also include Minimum error, M-loss, Gini impurity, and Bayes in v2 Figure 13. ConTree is added only to the literature overview.

E3.justification: V2 replaces uniform five-fold inner cross-validation with 20, 10, or five folds according to dataset size and tunes node count alone in the objective study. Tuning comparisons replace unequal fixed parameter lists with grids capped at k candidates, normally k=16, and extend the timeout from one to two hours. Synthetic feature noise changes from fixed-amplitude corruption of selected samples to variable-amplitude noise; class noise extends to 50%, and sample/feature grids also change.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled noise-by-sample-size analyses of objectives and tuning methods, linear-ground-truth robustness tests, tuning-budget sensitivity in Appendix B.3, and training-versus-test accuracy and binarization analyses in Appendix D. V1's separate objective comparison on 70 small datasets is removed. These changes substantially revise the questions tested and supporting diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly labels Section 5.4.2 summaries as mean plus/minus standard error, whereas v1 leaves its plus/minus statistic unspecified. New noise experiments report 1,000 repetitions and explicitly identify 95% confidence intervals in Figure 6. Literature-claim experiments still report 500 repetitions, without v1's stated 250-run depth-five exception; this establishes a reporting change, not independently verified additional runs. The Nemenyi and Wilcoxon framework remains.

E6.justification: Numerous scores, rankings, and findings are revised or added. Section 5.4.2 changes the reported ODT advantage over depth-matched CART from 1.1/1.3 percentage points at depths three/four to 1.3/1.0. These use changed benchmarks and protocols, so they are not same-setting performance changes. V2 adds noise, linear-separator, tuning-budget, and binarization results while removing v1's small-dataset objective results and detailed per-dataset SWA entries.

T1.justification: V2 removes the formal Error Gini and Error entropy definitions, changes Table 1's expected inequalities from strict to non-strict, and includes the probability-0.5 boundary in the splitting argument. Appendix B adds mathematical arguments about useful tuning-parameter bounds. The central concavity reasoning, retained loss definitions, and SWA formula and calculation procedure remain.

C1.justification: The claimed contributions shrink from four new objectives and three new tuning approaches to two each. More importantly, v1's central claim that the new losses outperform accuracy on small datasets is replaced by recommendations emphasizing existing regularizing objectives for noisy data; v2 acknowledges no significant advantage for M-loss and L-loss in its new noise experiments. The three overarching questions and six literature-claim verdicts remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains noisy-data benefits through additional regularization from Binom. and Minimum error, replacing v1's favorable interpretation of the new losses. It qualifies the question-length similarity claim for strong noise and explains why earlier studies missed this regime. Question-length tuning is no longer presented as generally promising, and new appendix discussion addresses binarization tradeoffs and inconclusive training/test curves.

D1.justification: The reproducibility specification is substantially revised through Appendix B's data-dependent parameter ranges, minimum steps, unconstrained settings, and candidate-selection rules. V2 also specifies accuracy rounding and rank ties, discloses Binom.'s alpha=0.25, clarifies CART's selection rule relative to RPart's one-standard-error rule, and adds dataset class-imbalance information. Hardware, the STreeD link, and the publication-time code-release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds related work on soft/oblique trees, continuous-feature ODTs, and discretization, including Brita, McTavish, and Piccialli, and cites Garey and Graham for worst-case question length. It removes the Branches citation by Chaouki et al. Most research positioning and the previous-comparison review remain, with the latter moved to Appendix C. Publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes existing material: objective definitions move to Appendix A, tuning descriptions to Appendix B, and detailed literature comparisons to Appendix C. Sections 3–5 are condensed and reorganized, the abstract and conclusions are rewritten, CART recommendations gain a dedicated block, and 'question length' replaces much of the 'expected depth' terminology.

P2.justification: Several result displays are redesigned and combined, including mean-performance and critical-distance panels in v2 Figures 4, 5, and 11. V1's detailed SWA table is replaced by a broader aggregate comparison in v2 Figure 13. New noise, sensitivity, training/test, binarization, and dataset-distribution figures are added, and the dataset table gains a class-imbalance column. These changes extend well beyond renumbering or relocation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind its practical recommendations. Controlled tuning budgets, linear-ground-truth experiments, and noise and binarization analyses address important limitations of v1's evaluation. The revision also qualifies its advocacy of new losses and identifies a strong-noise exception to question-length similarity. Some variant coverage and detailed per-dataset SWA results are lost, but the gains in experimental control, applicability testing, and evidence-calibrated recommendations outweigh those losses.
